               <ns0:p n="7">7 Which was with the <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Whether he was Pro-Consul, or Proprietor, it is in ef<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fect the same; for he it was that Governed the Island.</ns0:note> deputy of the coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trey Sergius Paulus, a prudent man; who called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">This desire was extraordinary, and wrought by God, in order to the fitting him for the further mercy of his Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />version, and Salvation; where such a desire is, it shall be granted: <ns0:hi>ask and ye shall have, Luke</ns0:hi> 11.9.</ns0:note> to hear the word of God.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 7.11. 2 Tim. 3.8.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">This is another name of him that was called <ns0:hi>Barje<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sus,</ns0:hi> which was not unusual, as <ns0:hi>Simon Bar-jonah, Matth.</ns0:hi> 16.17. This, <ns0:hi>Elymas</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> may be taken appe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>atively, and</ns0:note> Elymas the sorcerer (for <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">signifies the Magician or Sorcerer; but being it was a proper name unto others we read of, it may be so here.</ns0:note> so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn away the deputy from the faith.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">It is observable, that St. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> never before called this great Apostle by the name of <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi>: and henceforth never calls him by the name of <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi>; tho there be no great dif<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ference in these names. <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> might be more acceptable to the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> amongst whom hitherto he had conversed. And <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> a more pleasing name unto the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> unto whom he was now sent, and with whom for the future he should most converse. He was called <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> as he was a <ns0:hi>Iew</ns0:hi> born, an <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi>; and <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> as he was a Deni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son of <ns0:hi>Rome.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> having that name in good ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />count in several of their chief Families.</ns0:note> Then Saul (who also is <ns0:hi>called</ns0:hi> Paul) fil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Zeal for Gods Glory, and Faith and Power to work the ensuing Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />racle.</ns0:note> with the holy Ghost, set his eyes on him<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And said, O full of all subtilty and all <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> signifies a facility or readiness in doing mischief; and that such who are given to Sorcery are ea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sily drawn to commit any kind of sin whatsoever.</ns0:note> mischief, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matth. 13.38, John 8.44. 1 John 3.8.</ns0:note> thou <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause he did his work who is the <ns0:hi>Destroyer</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> in hindring what he could the Salvation of <ns0:hi>Sergius Paulus</ns0:hi> and his Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mily.</ns0:note> child of the devil, thou ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />my of all righteousness, wilt thou not cease <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">To make the way of God crooked, which is straight; and rugged, when indeed it is smooth: that is, to lay what rubs he could to keep any from coming un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to, or continuing in the ways of God.</ns0:note> to pervert the right ways of the Lord?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 And now behold, <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">The hand of the Lord is put for any powerful action of God, whether in Mercy or Judgment: here it is put for the Divine Power wherewith God strikes his Enemies.</ns0:note> the hand of the Lord <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not see<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the sun <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">God did in Judgment remember Mercy, inflicting this blindness only for a season, that it might be rather a Me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dicine than a punishment.</ns0:note> for a season. <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:389" />
went about, seeking some to lead him by the hand.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The Gospel which <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> Preached.</ns0:note> Then the deputy when he saw what was done, believed, being <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Finding in it (though a wise Man) depths beyond his fathoming: and all accompanied with such a power in doing of Mira<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cles, and changing of Hearts, and Lives; as might well amaze so prudent, and considering a man.</ns0:note> astonished at the doctrine of the Lord.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 Now when Paul and his company loosed from Paphos, they came to <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">A City in <ns0:hi>Pamphylia</ns0:hi>: not that there were any other Cities of that name; but because this Region was more commonly known, it being</ns0:note> Perga in <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">a Country in the lesser <ns0:hi>Asia,</ns0:hi> bordering on <ns0:hi>Cilicia.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Pamphy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lia: And John <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The departure of <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi>; of whom before, <ns0:hi>Verse</ns0:hi> 6. and <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 12.25. was blame-worthy, as <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 15.38. Some think he shunned that labour and suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fering which he saw attended the Gospel; others supposed that he returned to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> out of too fond an affection for his Mother, who lived there; and it may be that he re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />taining a great aversion from the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> might abhor to go amongst them: howsoever, <ns0:hi>let him that stands, take heed lest he fall.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> departing from them, returned to Jerusalem.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 ¶ But when they departed from Perga, they came to <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">So called to distinguish it from the other <ns0:hi>Antioch</ns0:hi> men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned in the first <ns0:hi>Verse,</ns0:hi> which was a City in <ns0:hi>Syria,</ns0:hi> as this in <ns0:hi>Pi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>idia,</ns0:hi> next to, or part of <ns0:hi>Pamphylia.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Antioch in Pisidia, and went in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to the synagouge <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Either to joyn with the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> in their worship, which was not then unlaw<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful, or to get an opportunity more publickly to Preach the Gospel unto them: they were no sooner come thither, but they mind that great business they went about.</ns0:note> on the sabbath-day, and sate down.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 And after the <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">The reading of the Law was commanded by <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>; and they say, that <ns0:hi>Ezra</ns0:hi> commanded the reading of the Prophets also in their Synagogues, which was used; as we may see in the 27th <ns0:hi>Verse.</ns0:hi> And so divided into several Secti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons, that once a Year they might be all read over.</ns0:note> reading of the law and the prophets, the <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">They were such as had the over-sight of this Service of God in their Synagogues, that it might be performed according to the prescription.</ns0:note> rulers of the Synagogue sent un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to them, saying, Ye men <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">An usual compellation which the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> gave one another, owning them to serve the same God, and professing a suitable respect for them.</ns0:note> brethren, If ye have any word of exhortation for the people <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">After the reading before spoken of, there followed a Sermon, or Exhortation; which the Apostles are desired to make, the Rulers of the Synagogue, as 'tis supposed, having had some previous knowledg of them.</ns0:note>, say on.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 Then Paul stood up <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">To procure silence and attention, as <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 12.17.</ns0:note>, and beckning with <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> hand, said, Men of Israel, and <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Besides the Native <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> the Proselytes, and such out of all Nations who left the Idolatry of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> and vow'd the only True God, met together in the worship of God; these were the <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> spoken of, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 17.4. It shews also what they are to do that would hear the Word of the Lord with profit; <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> to attend unto it in the fear of his Name.</ns0:note> ye that fear God, give audience.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 The <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">God was the God of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> after a peculiar manner.</ns0:note> God of this people of Israel <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Having chosen them before all Nations, to make him known unto them, to be served and worshipped by them.</ns0:note> chose our fathers, and <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">And God exalted them in the time of <ns0:hi>Ioseph</ns0:hi>; and whilst the memory of that great preservation wrought by his means, did continue, till another King arose that knew not <ns0:hi>Ioseph.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> exalted the people <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 1.1.</ns0:note>, when they dwelt as strangers in the land of Egypt, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 6.6. & 13.14, 16.</ns0:note> and with an <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The many Miracles done by the Power of God towards the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> deliverance out of <ns0:hi>Egypt.</ns0:hi> By which the Apostle would have them remember, that they owed all which they challenged from their Progenitors, to the Grace and Blessing of God only; and that God may do with his own as he please.</ns0:note> high arm brought he them out of it.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 16.35.</ns0:note> about the time of fourty years <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">This is Recorded, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 95.10. and remembred by the Apostle, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 3.8, 9. And to be admired through all Ages, that God should be so patient, or a People could be so perverse: some instead of <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, read <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, there being but one Letter difference, (and such as are usually changed into one another,) and then it speaks Gods providing for this People all that while, and carry<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing them as in his Bosom, as a Nurse bears the sucking Child, <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 11.12. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 1.31. or as an Eagle beareth her young ones on her Wings, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 32.11, 12. But it seems God did not bear with their Fathers, but destroyed them in the Wilderness, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10.5. First, God bare long with those that perished. Secondly, The succeeding Ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neration took not that warning which did become them, but followed their Fathers steps; and whilst one Genera<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion was wearing away, and another coming, this space of Forty years was spent, through the abundant compassion of God towards them; who did not consume them as they tempted him to do, in a moment.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Mac. 7.27. <ns0:hi>according to the</ns0:hi> 70. And so <ns0:hi>Chrysost<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> suffered he their manners in the wilderness.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And when he had destroyed <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">These seven Nations are mentioned, <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> 3.10.</ns0:note> seven na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions in the land of Canaan, he <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Josh. 14.1.</ns0:note> divided their land to them <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The Lot being disposed only as God would, <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 16. <ns0:hi>ult.</ns0:hi> And it was but reasonable that God having miracu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lously got this Land (for the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> did rather go to take possession of it, than to fight for it) and assumed a special right unto it, that he should divide it to whom he pleased, and in what proportions he thought good.</ns0:note> by lot.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And after that he gave <ns0:hi>unto them</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Judges 3.9.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">These Judges were persons deputed by God to govern and deliver that People; their Commission was attested usually by some extraordinary thing done by them, and their power (as being mediately from God) was absolute</ns0:note> judges, about the space of <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">The computation of years here mentioned, hath been very much controverted: That which hath the greatest probability with it, is, Either first, to have recourse to the 17 <ns0:hi>Verse,</ns0:hi> and begin this Aera there, with Gods chusing of their Fathers, and ending it at the time of the decision of the Land by lot, as <ns0:hi>Verse</ns0:hi> 19. for from the birth of <ns0:hi>Isaac,</ns0:hi> to this distribution of the Land, are reckoned 447 years; which may well be said here, About 450 years: but then the sense is, <ns0:hi>after that,</ns0:hi> such things mentioned in the 17, 18, 19. <ns0:hi>Verses</ns0:hi> were done; which were in the compass of 450 years, God then gave them Judges. Or, as others do refer these words to what follows, and begin the Aera or compu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tation from the going of the Children of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> out of <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> and ending it at the expulsion of the <ns0:hi>Iebusites</ns0:hi> out of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> which may make up this account: But then this passage of St. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> is not intended to shew how long the Judges Ruled, but when it was, or about what time that they Ruled; As also to shew what a long time it took up to gain that People a quiet possession of that promised Inheritance, their sins still keeping good things from them.</ns0:note> four hundred and fifty years, until Samuel the prophet.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And afterward they desired <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Their great sin in desiring a King was, because by that desire they rejected God, who had at that very time a Prophet <ns0:hi>(Samuel)</ns0:hi> by whom he governed them, 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 8.7. & 10.19. They had been under a Theocrasie ever since they came out of <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi>; their Laws, and their Gover<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nors being appointed by God; had their condition been as that of other Nations, their desire had not been a provo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation.</ns0:note> a king: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Sam. 8.5.</ns0:note> and God gave unto them Saul the son of Cis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, by the space of <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">These words, <ns0:hi>by the space of fourty years,</ns0:hi> are to be joyned with the foregoing <ns0:hi>Verse,</ns0:hi> and the other fore<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />going words in the <ns0:hi>Verse</ns0:hi> read with a Parenthesis: and thus they shew how long <ns0:hi>Samuel</ns0:hi> the Prophet (as he is here called) exercised his Prophetical Offices, which was the space here mentioned, partly before <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> was Anointed King, and in part afterward; in which, as another <ns0:hi>Moses,</ns0:hi> he cared for, and went in, and out, before the People of God, the like space of fourty years. This computation of St. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> might also agree more with the <ns0:hi>Septuagint,</ns0:hi> and be according to the then current account, which (not being of more consequence) St. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> would not controvert at this time, having greater matters to speak of unto them.</ns0:note> four<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty years.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And when <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">God had taken <ns0:hi>Saul</ns0:hi> away by death; for he would not suffer <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> to hasten it.</ns0:note> he had removed him, he raised up unto them <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Sam 16.13. Psal. 89.20, 21.</ns0:note> David to be their king, To whom also he gave testimony, and said, I have found David the <ns0:hi>son</ns0:hi> of Jesse, a man <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Favoured or beloved by me, and obedient to me; my servant, as God speaks of him, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 89.20.</ns0:note> after mine own heart, which shall fulfil <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">And here, that he should fulfil all Gods will, to wit, in governing his people; for he hath a Testi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monial upon record in Gods word, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 78.72.
